MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

PATIENT: [redacted name]

AGE/SEX: 59 year old female
SPECIMEN: Lymph node biopsy
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Lymph node biopsy evaluation for suspected BCL2 negative follicular lymphoma.

TEST PERFORMED:
Interphase FISH analysis for IGH/BCL2 rearrangement

METHODOLOGY:
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using MolecularPath IGH/BCL2 dual color dual fusion probe set. The IGH probe (14q32) is labeled with SpectrumGreen and the BCL2 probe (18q21) is labeled with SpectrumOrange. Analysis was correlated with BCL6 immunostained slide to identify appropriate cell population.

RESULTS:
IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement: NEGATIVE

Number of cells analyzed: 100
Number of cells with fusion signals: 0
Percentage positive: 0%

Normal signal pattern (2R2G) observed in all cells examined.

INTERPRETATION:
No evidence of IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)(q32;q21)] rearrangement detected by FISH analysis in the specimen examined. The absence of this translocation in the context of suspected follicular lymphoma is notable, as approximately 85-90% of follicular lymphomas harbor the t(14;18) translocation. BCL2-negative follicular lymphomas represent a distinct subset that may have different molecular drivers and clinical behavior.

Pathologist: [redacted name], MD
Electronically signed: [redacted date]
